Ransomware

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
A recent episode of the popular television series, “The Good Wife”, centred around what looked like a far-fetched scenario: a malware software worm is injected into the computers of law firm Lockhart Gardiner, a countdown clock begins, and the firm is given a 72 hour deadline to pay a ransom in the internet currency, Bitcoin, or lose all their data. Their software experts tell them there is no defence or cure – pay up or else.
This is the nightmare scenario that hit two prominent Cape Town professionals, top architect Jenny Mills and her husband, business consultant and IT developer, Chris Rumbell. They share office space and a computer network. Chris clicked on an email that had executable file (.exe attachment) and within seconds the dreaded worm, Cryptolocker, had infected their system. What happens is you can see your files and information but you can’t access them.

Further information:
Each victim is hit by an individual code and by paying the “ransom” in Bit coins the criminal can’t be traced. The message says you have 1 week to pay 500 Dollars and then if you haven’t paid it goes up to 1000 dollars to be paid within 96 hours and on it goes. Once you pay the money you still aren’t sure you will be able to access your data. The impact on small business is devastating. One case study, a graphic artists lost all her work.
There are various versions of this “Ransomware” doing the rounds, including Cryptowall, but they all share one characteristic – their file encryption programme uses such a sophisticated and complicated algorithm that no cyber-security experts have yet been able to combat it. The most effective way to defeat ransomware is to have a regularly updated backup routine in place, says Nathan Loftie-Eaton, security specialist at computer security firm, ESET SA.
Mills and Rumbell were lucky – they had recently backed up their system, so damage was minimal and they avoided paying the ransom to have their files unencrypted, which starts off at around four bitcoins (one bitcoin currently trades at around R3 700.00), but then the price escalates.
The original Cryptolocker programme was shut down last year, but by then had earned close to US3-million in ransom, Dell Counter Threat Unit (CTU) experts estimated. But there are many mutant variants doing the rounds, and they are now hitting South African email users. The original code is said to be available on the “Dark Web” as open source, meaning any crooked programmer with enough knowledge can modify it to their own ends.
In the USA, the Crytowall programmed infected over 600 000 computer systems in the last six months of 2014 and held 5 billion files hostage, earning its creators more than $1 million, the Dell CTU researchers found. They called it “the largest and most destructive ransomware threat on the Internet”.
We speak to victims of encryption attacks and ransom attempts, and to the experts tracking the data kidnappers. They will also tell viewers what steps they can take to safeguard their computers and their networks. It will inform people about the “darkweb” and other major cybercrime and how its impacting small business.

Press Release:


Ransomware
Imagine being on a critical deadline and opening your computer, only to find all your files locked. A message appears to tell you that paying up is the only way to free your files. The ransom? US$500. It’s a virus called CryptoLocker and it’s eating its way through South African computers and backup systems. Carte Blanche asks: who is behind the malicious infection and what should you do if you fall victim?


Script:


Link “Imagine sitting down and at your computer to complete some vital work and realising that all your files have been frozen then a message pops up on the screen that reads the structure and data within your files have been irrevocably changed you will not be able to work with them, read them or see them it’s the same thing as losing them forever
Louise “ You are actually held to ransom for your own work and my ransom was 500 dollars and then there is a timer which starts counting down and it says after that time your files are gone forever and basically it says don’t try anything because they are the only ones that can help you
Script: Cyptolocker – it’s the IT version of Ebola. It releases a virus onto your computer when you open an email with an attachment or a link to a website. And, it’s so cleverly disguised – something that graphic artist Louise Swoboda discovered to her horror.
Louis “I was sitting working and this email came in and I opened it up and it was a zip file and I saw the unzipping and straight away I thought something was wrong and I shut down and went back on with my work and I didn’t think anything of it .And the next morning I sat down to do my work ….and suddenly all my files wouldn’t open
Chris Rumbell “We had sent out the day before to all our suppliers an email saying please send us your statements. An email came in which said your July 2015 statement. We pay for virus scanning we are not using a free addition here so the virus scanner came up scanned, which was very quick and then said restart your computer now that is the thing that causes the virus to start
John “You have asked us to disguise your identity what are your concerns?”
Chris Rumbell “We feel that the stigma attached and the perception of our clients to what has happened here could put us at business risk “
Link “Ransomware has been around for at least the last two years but there appears to be a recent surge in attacks the victims are often small or medium sized companies that loose vital data even if they have the necessary backups in place”
Chris Rumbell “It works first with the computer you are working with now we don’t store any of our information on our computers everything is stored on a central area on the server so it managed to get through that computer pretty quick and then it jumped onto our network attached storage and it started working in there. It managed to get through one of our NAS we have got 3 which is why we were able to recover reasonably quickly”
Script: ESET is a global antivirus software company. CEO Carey van Vlaandern says that there has been an 80% increase of attacks on their clients in the last few months
Carey “You as a user may get an email from your friend and it looks legitimate and if you are not looking at the file extension you may run the ransomware and it’s not like you have been negligent it’s just how they spoof the email. We have our virus lab in Slovakia and they are dealing with about 250 000 viruses a day that’s the number of new attacks that you are susceptible to daily.
Script: Ransomware attacks both Mac and PC users. But why isn’t your internet service provider intercepting them or your antivirus software
Carey ”Antivirus is not actually supposed to stop ransomware because of the nature of how the virus is written. The files is coming through as legitimate windows files so if we do that to our clients we would have a lot more upset clients if we were stopping their businesses running”
Script: AIG’s head of Africa division for Cyber insurance Philip Hobson says cybercrime is costing the global economy 100s of billions of dollars annually
John” If insurance companies have cyber divisions it is testament to the gravity of the risk”
Philip Hobson “It’s the largest risks that corporations face these days. Our indications are that SA being part of an emerging market is definitely more at risk than other economies “
Script: You can see your work but you can’t open it until you pay the ransom
Chris Rumbell “You can pay 1.3 bitcoins today and we will unlock your files now a bitcoin it internet money but you don’t pay with a credit card there you go to a bitcoin trader you and set up a bitcoin monitor on your machine and then you pay them so it’s completely untraceable. If you don’t respond within 72 hours to their ransom request they will then double the price until after a month when they will delete what they call the private encryption key so you can never decrypt your files again
Link 12 05 36 07 Ransomware lurks in the hidden part of the internet known as the dark web it’s a mysterious space that some experts say could be 10 times larger than the so called surface web that’s the part of the internet that you and I use
Script Johann Combrinck from IT company Space Age technologies says the Dark Web is like a parallel universe where mostly illegal activities like drug and child trafficking takes place. People operate there completely anonymously and are untraceable
Johann “You need very specialised tools and software to operate in the dark web. It’s also typically where the ransomware is created and sold
John “They are fools behind these things”
Johann “You have got very clever people working together, so they collaborate. It’s not just a single person or a single company it’s a group of people with the same intent “
Philip Hobson “The motives for attacking is either money or intellectual property and in the case of ransomware is largely money”
Johann “The CIA and NSIA often speak of how terrorism is funded, it’s funded by mechanism like these
Script: It’s impossible to know who is winning this cyber war because people don’t admit to have been attacked
Johan “It’s difficult for people to admit if something like his has happened. They got reputation damage by not being able to transact so it’s not only reputation there are real operational costs
Philip Hobson “The experience we have had around the losses certainly the public companies the negative impact on the reputation can be enormous and if it is not managed at an executive level it could affect even the share price of the business”
Script: There is no point in reporting this extortion to your local SAP’s branch and currently there is only insurance for large corporates. It’s hitting small to medium businesses the hardest.
Louis “You are looking at around 60 R 70 000 “
Chris Rumbell “The amount of time and effort and energy its cost this business close on R 100 000
Script: Most people are tempted to pay the ransom and clearly many do otherwise these guys would stop creating new viruses
Chris Rumbell “Potentially that is not a lot of money to pay to get our information back its worth a lot more than 500 US Dollars. But you are also funding for people to replicate this even further
Carey “You are paying with your credit card to some cyber-criminal who might not even give your information back”
Philip Hobson “The more you hear about it the scarier you get and if you are not worried about it I would say you are a little bit uninformed”
Link “Most of us know about the importance of backing up but how many of us have made it part of our daily routine well many businesses often fall into the same trap but it is at that point that they get hit
Louis “Unfortunately for me that month I hadn’t backed up so it really hit me hard but if I had plugged my backup in that day it would have wiped out over a year’s work”
Carey “The cyrptolocker can even attack external hard drives say for example you even have your cloud drive mapped onto your machine it can attack that too the threat landscape is very big it’s not enough to just have back up or just have antivirus you have to make sure you are covered in various different ways
Johann “The first thing you have to do is switch off your machine don’t try and plug it into the corporate network or try and fix it yourself the longer the thing stays on the worse it gets
Script: All you can do is pull the plug and call a professional to wipe your computer and reinstall everything from scratch.
